origins.section: 13.1. PCI DSS Covers Every System That Touches Card Data, and Every System That Can Reach One
13.3. Card Data Ends Up Where Nobody Meant to Store It
13.5. A Scanner Finding Is a Question, and the Answer Is Written Down
13.7. Data Protection Law Covers the Same Records and Can Ask for the Opposite

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-build-server-scope: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-build-server-scope: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-build-server-scope: 13.1: the CI server holds no card data but is in scope because whoever controls it controls the switch, and it can ship a build that copies every card number.
recorded.prompt:q-empty-queue-on-disk: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-empty-queue-on-disk: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-empty-queue-on-disk: 13.3: after the cloned reversal is taken out the file still holds the card numbers, track 2 and the PIN block, stored with each byte's top bit flipped, so a plain text scan finds nothing.
recorded.prompt:q-critical-but-unexposed: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-critical-but-unexposed: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-critical-but-unexposed: 13.5: when triage shows the finding doesn't apply to this system it is deferred with a written risk acceptance naming an owner, a review date and the event that would reopen it.
recorded.prompt:q-erasure-and-retention: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-erasure-and-retention: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-erasure-and-retention: 13.7: the keyed lookup of unit s9 finds a card's encrypted records without storing its number in clear.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-build-server-scope:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-build-server-scope:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-build-server-scope:b: 13.1: the page says the CI server holds no card data and puts it in scope for control over the switch, not for data passing through it.
recorded.prompt:q-build-server-scope:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-build-server-scope:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-build-server-scope:c: 13.1: counting only systems that store card numbers is the team's named mistake, which leaves the CI server without controls and is reported as a scope gap.
recorded.prompt:q-build-server-scope:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-build-server-scope:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-build-server-scope:d: 13.1 (and 13.11): scope covers every system that can affect the CDE's security, which signing does not change, though the page never mentions signing or review, so this is implied rather than stated.
recorded.prompt:q-empty-queue-on-disk:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-empty-queue-on-disk:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-empty-queue-on-disk:a: 13.3: taking an entry out appends a deletion, and the old bytes stay until the cleaner deletes the file.
recorded.prompt:q-empty-queue-on-disk:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-empty-queue-on-disk:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-empty-queue-on-disk:b: 13.3: the plain scan reported card numbers [], and the page says a text-only scan would have reported this file clean.
recorded.prompt:q-empty-queue-on-disk:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-empty-queue-on-disk:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-empty-queue-on-disk:c: 13.3: the store flips the top bit for sort order rather than encrypting, and the clone left track 2 and the PIN block as well as the card numbers.
recorded.prompt:q-critical-but-unexposed:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-critical-but-unexposed:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-critical-but-unexposed:b: 13.5: closing it instead of deferring means nobody looks again when the exposure changes.
recorded.prompt:q-critical-but-unexposed:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-critical-but-unexposed:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-critical-but-unexposed:c: 13.5: overriding is the fix for a finding that applies, and a rushed override days before certification can change serialization, TLS defaults or the classpath, although the override is a legitimate tool, just not here.
recorded.prompt:q-critical-but-unexposed:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-critical-but-unexposed:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-critical-but-unexposed:d: 13.5: severity alone doesn't decide, and a rushed upgrade before certification carries its own risk in the payment path.
recorded.prompt:q-erasure-and-retention:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-erasure-and-retention:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-erasure-and-retention:a: 13.7: pseudonymise with keyed values, not plain hashes, which unit s9 reverses in a quarter of a second.
recorded.prompt:q-erasure-and-retention:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-erasure-and-retention:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-erasure-and-retention:c: 13.7 with 13.4: the tables hold the number only encrypted, so a clear search finds none of those records, though 13.7 also asks you to find the person's data in logs, queues and backups, where a clear-number scan (13.2) is useful, so the option is partly true.
recorded.prompt:q-erasure-and-retention:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-erasure-and-retention:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-erasure-and-retention:d: 13.7: a masked number can't find a card's records because its six and four digits are shared by many cards.
